text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia may announce his government line-up tomorrow (Monday).

- Negotiations between Ouyahia and main party leaders to forge a consensus on the cabinet line-up continue. Parties are still divided over the number of portfolios each political group is claiming in the cabinet.

- A statement on the government formation was postponed and Ouyahia will have hard negotiations today. Former ruling National Liberation Front (FLN) and Islamist-oriented Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS) want half of the govenment posts which total about 31 ministries and secretary of state positions.

- Consensus over forming two parliamentary commissions in the National Assembly (lower house) showed start of a political alliance between MPS and National Democratic Rally (RND) which groups President Liamine Zeroual's supporters.
- An International Monetary Fund (IMF) official says Algeria needs no more debt rescheduling.
